title: Anthropic pilots Claude for Chrome and publishes prompt-injection attack success rates
summary: Anthropic began piloting Claude in Chrome, a browser extension that lets trusted users instruct Claude to see the page, click buttons and fill forms on their behalf, with 1,000 Max plan users from a waitlist; the research preview shipped site-level permissions that users can grant or revoke, confirmations before high-risk actions such as publishing, purchasing or sharing personal data, blocked site categories (financial services, adult content, pirated content) and improved system-prompt instructions, while classifiers for suspicious instruction patterns and unusual data-access requests were still being built and tested. In Anthropic's red-team evaluation of 123 test cases across 29 attack scenarios, browser use without safety mitigations showed a 23.6% attack success rate, which the mitigations added to autonomous mode reduced to 11.2%, and on a challenge set of four browser-specific attack types the rate fell from 35.7% to 0%; before mitigations, a malicious email posing as a security request that said no additional confirmation was required led Claude to delete the user's emails, which the mitigated version recognised as likely phishing and did not act on.
verification_note: URL fetched 2026-10-17 (live page).
